summary: Angela Falco Howard works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. She completed her doctoral dissertation at New York University under Alexander Coburn Soper and studied under Yoshito S. Hakeda. She was attested as a professor at Rutgers University in 2005.
Angela Manderscheid is a scholar in Tibetology and other fields. She held posts at the Free University of Berlin and at the University of Oulu, where she was attested as a researcher in 1998.

Angela Sumegi specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She earned her Ph.D. from the University of Ottawa and studied under Nalini Devdas. In 2008, she was attested as an assistant professor at Carleton University's College of the Humanities.

Angela Zito is a scholar of religious studies and Sinology who completed her Ph.D. at the University of Chicago (~1980–1989). She became an associate professor at New York University in 1999 and founded Positions: Asia Critique and New York University.

Philosopher Angelika Krebs studied at Freiburg, New College, Konstanz, UC Berkeley, and Goethe University Frankfurt under Bernard Williams. She held posts at Konstanz, Frankfurt, and Basel, alongside visiting appointments at Freiburg, Zurich, Princeton, and Munich.

Angelika Malinar works in Indology and religious studies. She studied at Mainz and Tübingen, completing her PhD and Habilitation there. She served as Dozentin at Free University of Berlin and SOAS, and became Außerordentliche Professorin für Indologie at Zurich in 2009.

Angelo Brelich (1913–1977) was a scholar in religious studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at Erzsébet University from ~1933 to 1937 and held a post at Sapienza University of Rome from ~1958 to 1977.

Angelo De Gubernatis (1840–1913) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Turin and Berlin under Bopp and Weber. He held professorships at the University of Florence (1863–1891) and Sapienza University of Rome (1890–1908).

Angelo Francesco Saverio Maffei (1844–1899) was an Indologist and linguist educated at Seminario Maggiore Arcivescovile di Trento and the Pontifical Gregorian University. He served as rector of St Aloysius College (1891–1896) and was a Fellow of the University of Madras.

Angelo Maria Pizzagalli (1883–1944) was an Indologist who studied at the University of Pisa (~1903–1907) under Carlo Formichi. He later taught Sanskrit at the University of Pisa (1913), University of Genoa (1914), and University of Milan (~1924–1944).
Anil Kumar specializes in computational linguistics and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Hyderabad by 2012 and held a post there.

Anil Vidyalankar (b. 1928) is an Indologist, philosopher, and linguist. He studied at Gurukula Kangri Vishwavidyalaya, Columbia University, and the University of Delhi. He founded Sandhaan in 1988, serving as its director as attested in 1999.

Animesh Prakash works in Indology and Buddhist studies. After earning an MA at the University of Hong Kong (2016–2017), he served as Assistant Professor at Somaiya Vidyavihar University (2014–2018) and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (2018).

Animesh Roy is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He completed an integrated MA in Sanskrit at Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda Educational and Research Institute (2017–2022) and became a Research Scholar at Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit in 2022.
Animisha Tewari works in philosophy and Indology. She completed a Bachelor of Arts at Miranda House (2017–2020) and a Master of Arts at the University of Delhi (2020–2022).

Anirban Dash works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He held positions at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 2003–2005 and 2026) and Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 2021).
Anita is an Indologist who earned her Ph.D. at the University of Lucknow. In 2009, she held a post as Professor at Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith.

Anjay Dhanawade is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Mumbai, Savitribai Phule Pune University, and Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth (Ph.D. 2010–2016), and was an assistant professor at Lokavikas Samajik Sanstha (2010–2023).

Ankita Chakraborty is an Indology scholar who studied under doctoral supervisor Bijoya Goswami (attested 2026). She held a post as a Research Scholar / Fellow at The Asiatic Society, attested in 2026.
Ankita Nanda is an Indology scholar who earned her Ph.D. from Panjab University in 2022, where she also held a post as Senior Research Scholar in 2022.
